problems.title: An absolute difference in ticket cost
problems.question: Five tickets must cost within 4 lari of 80 lari. Model the allowed ticket price x.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Within d of c means absolute difference at most d.
steps: Total cost is 5x, so require |5x−80|≤4. Equivalently 76≤5x≤84, giving 15.2≤x≤16.8.

problems.title: Perimeter of a region between two rays
problems.question: Find the perimeter defined by 0≤x≤2,0≤y≤2,x≤2y,y≤2x.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: The sloping boundaries are y=x/2 and y=2x.
steps: The polygon vertices are (0,0),(2,1),(2,2),(1,2). The two sloping edges have lengths √5 each, and the other two edges lengths 1 each.
The perimeter is 2+2√5.

problems.title: A proportional radical cancels out
problems.question: Evaluate $(a+b)[(a+b)/b-(a-b)/a]\div(a+b^2/a)$ when a=20% of √199 and b=35% of √199.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: The bracket is $(a^2+b^2)/(ab)$; the final divisor is $(a^2+b^2)/a$.
steps: The expression simplifies to (a+b)/b=1+a/b. Both inputs are positive, so cancellation is valid.
a/b=20/35=4/7, hence the result is 11/7.

problems.title: A doubled trapezoid angle fixes its base difference
problems.question: Trapezoid ABCD has smaller base BC=b, leg AB=a and ABC=2CDA. Find larger base AD.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Draw BE parallel to CD, meeting AD; then ED=BC. Angle equalities make ABE isosceles.
steps: Put CDA=theta. Because BE is parallel to CD, CBE=theta, so ABE=ABC−CBE=theta.
Also AEB=theta, hence AE=AB=a. The parallelogram BCDE gives ED=b.
Thus AD=AE+ED=a+b.

problems.title: Find the whole secant length
problems.question: A circle has radius 2; an exterior point is distance 4 from its centre. The inside secant length is 2 less than the outside length. Find the whole secant.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Point power $=4^2-2^2=12$; outside × whole = power.
steps: Let the outside length be t, so inside=t−2 and whole=2t−2. Then t(2t−2)=12.
t²−t−6=(t−3)(t+2)=0. Positivity gives t=3, inside=1, whole=4.

problems.title: Rational and irrational conjugate expressions
problems.question: Let A=(2+√3)²+(2−√3)², B=(2+√3)³+(2−√3)³, C=(2+√3)²(2−√3)³. Which are irrational?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: The two conjugates have sum 4 and product 1.
steps: A=4²−2=14. B=4³−3×1×4=52. Both are integers.
C equals the square of their product times (2−√3), so C=2−√3, irrational.

problems.title: Average speed over equal distances
problems.question: A car covers half its distance at V and half at U, with positive unequal speeds. Find its overall average speed.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Average speed = total distance / total time.
steps: For total distance 2d, time is d/V+d/U. The average is $2d/[d(1/V+1/U)]=2/(1/V+1/U)$.

problems.title: Percentage change after taking a square root
problems.question: x>0 increases by 96%. By what percentage does √(x/5) increase?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: The new x is 1.96x; square roots multiply by √1.96.
steps: √1.96=1.4, so the new quantity is 140% of the old one. Its increase is 40%.

problems.title: Two upper-angle bisectors meet on the lower base
problems.question: Trapezoid ABCD has height 12. Bisectors of the obtuse angles at B,C meet at K on AD, with BK=13,CK=15. Find AD.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Angle-bisector and parallel-line equalities give AK=AB and DK=CD.
steps: Use K=(0,0), B=(−5,12), C=(9,12), from √(13²−12²)=5 and √(15²−12²)=9. These are the inward-bisector positions.
If AK=p, equality AB=AK gives (p−5)²+144=p², hence p=169/10=16.9.
If DK=q, equality CD=DK gives (q−9)²+144=q², hence q=225/18=12.5.

problems.title: Squared tangent and cotangent
problems.question: Evaluate tan²60°+cot²60°.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: The squared sum is 3+1/3=10/3.

problems.title: Cancellation in a radical expression
problems.question: Evaluate $3\sqrt x/x-(3+\sqrt x)/\sqrt x+x$ at x=101.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: For x>0, √x/x=1/√x.
steps: The first two terms simplify to 3/√x−3/√x−1=−1. Thus the expression is x−1=100.

problems.title: Order powers of a negative fraction
problems.question: Order a,a²,a³ for a=−√(1/2).
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: −1<a<0 implies a<a³<0<a².
steps: Multiplying a negative number by its square, a factor between 0 and 1, moves it toward zero, so a³>a. The square a² is positive.

problems.title: The closest listed approximation to a square root
problems.question: Which listed value is closest to √7:2,2.2,√5,2.4,2.6,2.8?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Compare absolute differences.
steps: √7≈2.64575 and √5≈2.23607. Its distance to 2.6 is about 0.04575, less than the distances to the other choices (the next closest,2.8,is about 0.15425 away).

problems.title: Ratio of external and internal tangent segments
problems.question: Circle radii are 1 and 2 and centre distance 4. Find external-tangent/internal-tangent segment length.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: The lengths are √15 and √7. Their ratio is √(15/7), with both tangents existing since 4>3.

problems.title: Product of two hypotenuse projections
problems.question: A right triangle’s legs are 2 and 3. Find the product of their projections on the hypotenuse.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: The hypotenuse is c=√13; projected lengths are a²/c and b²/c.

problems.title: Use the root equation to reduce squares
problems.question: a,b are roots of x²−5x−2=0. Evaluate 2a²+b²−6a−b.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Each root satisfies t²=5t+2 and a+b=5.
steps: The expression becomes 2(5a+2)+(5b+2)−6a−b=4a+4b+6.
Using a+b=5 gives 26, independent of root ordering.

problems.title: A quadratic with two explicit parameter roots
problems.question: For which a does x²−(a+1)x+a=0 have two distinct real roots?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: The factorization is (x−1)(x−a).
steps: The roots are 1 and a, both real for every real a. They are distinct exactly when a≠1.

problems.title: Count roots after an absolute-value substitution
problems.question: How many real roots satisfy x²−2x+1=|x−1|?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Put t=|x−1|≥0; then t²=t.
steps: t=0 gives x=1. t=1 gives x=0,2. There are three distinct roots.

problems.title: Perimeter from circumradius and angles
problems.question: A triangle has angles alpha,beta,gamma and circumradius R. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Extended sine rule: a=2R sin alpha, and similarly for b,c.
steps: Add the three side formulas to obtain the perimeter.

problems.title: Perimeter from inradius and angles
problems.question: A triangle has angles alpha,beta,gamma and inradius r. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: The tangent length from a vertex of angle alpha is r cot(alpha/2).
steps: Each side is the sum of its endpoint tangent lengths. The full perimeter counts each vertex tangent length twice.
Thus P=2r[cot(alpha/2)+cot(beta/2)+cot(gamma/2)].

problems.title: Factor a quadratic by splitting the middle term
problems.question: Factor 3x²+5x−8.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Write 5x=8x−3x and group.

problems.title: Remainder at a linear divisor’s zero
problems.question: Find the remainder of x⁴−x³+x²−x+1 divided by x+2.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: The remainder is P(−2).

problems.title: Build a quadratic from two irrational roots
problems.question: Which equation has roots 1−√2 and 2+√2?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: A monic quadratic is x²−(root sum)x+(root product)=0.
steps: The sum is 3 and the product is −√2. Thus the equation is x²−3x−√2=0.

problems.title: An angle at a bisector’s foot
problems.question: AB=6,BC=8,AC=7 and BK bisects B. Find cos BKC.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Angle-bisector theorem; $BK^2=AB\,BC[1-AC^2/(AB+BC)^2]$; cosine rule.
steps: AK:KC=6:8=3:4, so AK=3,KC=4. The bisector formula gives BK²=48(1−49/196)=36, hence BK=6.

problems.title: Median length from three sides
problems.question: AB=6,BC=8,AC=7. Find median BM.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: $BM=\tfrac12\sqrt{2AB^2+2BC^2-AC^2}$.
steps: The quantity under the root is 72+128−49=151. Thus BM=√151/2.
